note: Terms module-03 introduces, and the lesson responsible for teaching each. Enforced by scripts/lint-glossary.mjs. Harbor was assumed to be the friendly module because everyone has started a job; a 2026-08-22 audit measured SLA used in 8 lessons, provisioning in 13, escalation in 9, and none of them defined. No module is glossary-free. Keep ASCII-only.

terms.gloss: Service level agreement: the promised deadline for a task - 'a laptop is ordered within one business day'. It turns 'soon' into a date a machine can check.
Setting up everything a new hire needs before day one: account, email, badge, laptop, payroll. Provisioning is the work; the plan is the list of it.
The governed list of what a given job title gets. Hiring a Warehouse Associate expands to the same set every time, which is what makes onboarding automatable.
A named bundle of permissions. People are added to groups rather than granted permissions one by one, so access can be audited and removed cleanly.
Grant exactly what the role profile lists and nothing more. A convenient extra grant is a policy exception, not a favor.
Start Date, used as an anchor: SD-1 is the day before the hire starts, SD+2 the second day after. Every deadline is written relative to SD so a moved start date recomputes the whole plan.
Safe to run twice. Running an idempotent step again converges on the same result instead of creating a second account. Check-then-create, never create-blindly.
A point where parallel branches have to converge before anything continues - a fan-in. The readiness gate holds until every provisioning task is done, so one blocked laptop blocks the hire.
Handing a stuck task upward on a schedule, to a named person, with a deadline. An escalation without an owner and a clock is just a complaint.
A temporary substitute (here, a spare laptop) that unblocks day one while the real item is still coming. The workaround is recorded, not hidden.
Shipping a deliberately incomplete package and stating what is missing and why, rather than delaying everything or pretending it is complete.
